content.thinking: Found it: V2 expects lowercase input but categorise passes raw words, so the fix is to lowercase titles inside categorise before passing to the model, which is safe for V1 too. I should test with something like "Kettle in brushed steel" against V2 to confirm it confidently predicts Kitchen, and double-check the callers of categorise still match its unchanged signature.
Found a case mismatch: V2's vocabulary is lowercase but wasn't receiving lowercased input from `categorise`. I've fixed it by lowercasing the title before passing it to the model.

input.explanation:
Everything below describes the code on main. Revision 7c3ca00c, which was running when the alert fired, isn't in main's history, and I haven't read it. I'm assuming its `categorising.py` matches main's, but I haven't checked.

**The fault (src/io_shop/categorising.py on main).** `CategoriserModel.predict` only lowercases a word when `lowercases_its_input` is True. V1 sets it to True; V2 sets it to False. The file's own comment says V2's tokeniser "moved out of the model and into the training pipeline, which lowercases every title" before the vocabulary was built. So V2 only recognises lowercase words like "kettle" and "keyboard". But `categorise` passed `title.split()` straight to the model, so the shop never did the step the training pipeline did. Under V2, any capitalised word ("Kettle in brushed steel", "KEYBOARD with backlight") fails to match. If no word in the title is all-lowercase and known, the purchase falls through to "General" with `confident=False`. Nothing fails, so error rate and latency stay flat while the confident share drops. That fits the rule_reading fall from 0.91 to 0.42.

**Why this is a code fault, not just a bad model.** The model does what its comment says. The shop-side code never did the input preparation V2 depends on. Rolling back to v1 only hides the problem; switching `categoriser.model` back to v2 would bring it straight back.

**The change.** `categorise` now lowercases the title before splitting it and passing it to the model.
- V1: unchanged, because it already lowercases each word itself and lowercasing twice changes nothing.
- V2: words now arrive in the case its vocabulary was trained on.

Nothing else in the repository calls `predict` (I searched for it), and `categorise`'s signature is unchanged. `predict` itself is unchanged, so `lowercases_its_input` still means what it says.

**The test (tests/io_shop/test_categorising.py).** The new test asserts that V2 files capitalised titles ("Kettle in brushed steel", "KEYBOARD with backlight", "Fitness Smartwatch") under the right category with confidence. Against the old `categorise` it should fail: none of those titles has a lowercase word V2 knows, so each would come back as "General" with no confidence. A second test checks that V1 and V2 agree on capitalised titles. That is the check that was missing when the upgrade went out: the existing V2 tests only covered titles whose matching word was already lowercase.

files.content:
"""Filing a purchase under a category - what the monthly statement's breakdown reads.

A purchase reaches the shop as the title the shopper saw and nothing else, and a
model decides which aisle it belongs in. Most titles name the thing outright -
a kettle, a backpack, a novel - so the model is a vocabulary rather than anything
cleverer: a title is split into words, and the first word the model knows says
where the purchase goes. A title it knows no word of is filed under "General",
which is where a shop's own catalogue puts anything it has not classified, and
the filing says the model was not confident of it.

That last part is the figure worth watching. A purchase filed under "General" is
not an error - nothing fails, the page renders, the shopper is charged what they
were charged - so the only sign a model has stopped recognising the catalogue is
how much of it it is still confident about.

Which model files a purchase arrives here already decided, the way every other
choice the deployment makes does. The versions live in this module; which one the
shop loads is the deployment's business - see `categoriser.model` in
`deploy/values-production.yaml`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Final

# Where a purchase goes when the model recognises nothing in its title - the
# catalogue's own name for unclassified, and the default a `Purchase` carries.
UNCATEGORISED: Final = "General"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Categorisation:
    """Where one purchase was filed, and whether the model knew why."""

    category: str
    confident: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CategoriserModel:
    """One trained version of the categoriser.

    `vocabulary` maps a word to the category it files a purchase under, spelled as
    the model was trained on it. `lowercases_its_input` is whether the model folds
    the case of the words it is handed before looking them up, or takes them
    exactly as given.
    """

    version: str
    vocabulary: Mapping[str, str]
    lowercases_its_input: bool

    def predict(self, words: Sequence[str]) -> Categorisation:
        """The category of the first word this model knows, or `UNCATEGORISED`
        with no confidence when it knows none of them."""
        for word in words:
            looked_up = word.lower() if self.lowercases_its_input else word
            category = self.vocabulary.get(looked_up)

            if category is not None:
                return Categorisation(category=category, confident=True)

        return Categorisation(category=UNCATEGORISED, confident=False)


_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY: Final[Mapping[str, str]] = {
    "headphones": "Audio",
    "speaker": "Audio",
    "keyboard": "Computing",
    "monitor": "Computing",
    "mouse": "Computing",
    "kettle": "Kitchen",
    "toaster": "Kitchen",
    "blender": "Kitchen",
    "lamp": "Home",
    "blanket": "Home",
    "backpack": "Travel",
    "suitcase": "Travel",
    "jacket": "Clothing",
    "trainers": "Clothing",
    "novel": "Books",
    "cookbook": "Books",
    "charger": "Accessories",
    "cable": "Accessories",
}

# The first model the shop ran. It folds case itself, so whatever reaches it is
# matched however the title happened to be capitalised.
V1: Final = CategoriserModel(
    version="v1",
    vocabulary=_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY,
    lowercases_its_input=True,
)

# The upgrade, retrained on a catalogue that had grown two product lines since the
# first. Its tokeniser moved out of the model and into the training pipeline,
# which lowercases every title before the vocabulary is built - so the model now
# takes words exactly as it is given them, and is smaller and quicker for it.
V2: Final = CategoriserModel(
    version="v2",
    vocabulary={
        **_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY,
        "smartwatch": "Wearables",
        "earbuds": "Audio",
    },
    lowercases_its_input=False,
)

# Every version the shop can load, by the name the deployment selects it with.
MODELS: Final[Mapping[str, CategoriserModel]] = {
    model.version: model for model in (V1, V2)
}


def categorise(title: str, model: CategoriserModel) -> Categorisation:
    """Where `model` files a purchase with this title.

    The title is lowercased here, before any model sees it, because that is how
    every model's vocabulary was built: v1 folds case itself, but v2's tokeniser
    moved into the training pipeline and v2 takes words exactly as given. Doing
    the fold here keeps the shop's input in the shape the model was trained on,
    whichever version the deployment selects.
    """
    return model.predict(title.lower().split())

from __future__ import annotations

from io_shop.categorising import MODELS, UNCATEGORISED, V1, V2, categorise

"""Where the categoriser files a purchase, and whether it was sure.

A regression net for the shop's own models, written after them. Each case is a
title the catalogue could carry and the aisle it belongs in.
"""


def test_the_first_model_files_a_title_by_the_word_it_knows() -> None:
    filed = categorise("Kettle in brushed steel", V1)

    assert filed.category == "Kitchen"
    assert filed.confident


def test_the_first_model_reads_a_word_however_it_is_capitalised() -> None:
    assert categorise("KEYBOARD with backlight", V1).category == "Computing"
    assert categorise("Wireless mouse", V1).category == "Computing"


def test_a_title_with_no_word_the_model_knows_is_filed_under_general() -> None:
    filed = categorise("Gift card", V1)

    assert filed.category == UNCATEGORISED
    assert not filed.confident


def test_the_first_model_does_not_know_the_newer_product_lines() -> None:
    assert not categorise("Fitness smartwatch", V1).confident


def test_the_upgrade_knows_the_newer_product_lines() -> None:
    assert categorise("Fitness smartwatch", V2).category == "Wearables"
    assert categorise("Wireless earbuds", V2).category == "Audio"


def test_the_upgrade_files_everything_the_first_model_did_the_same_way() -> None:
    assert categorise("Portable speaker", V2).category == "Audio"
    assert categorise("Family cookbook", V2).category == "Books"


def test_the_upgrade_reads_a_word_however_it_is_capitalised() -> None:
    kettle = categorise("Kettle in brushed steel", V2)
    assert kettle.category == "Kitchen"
    assert kettle.confident

    keyboard = categorise("KEYBOARD with backlight", V2)
    assert keyboard.category == "Computing"
    assert keyboard.confident

    watch = categorise("Fitness Smartwatch", V2)
    assert watch.category == "Wearables"
    assert watch.confident


def test_both_models_agree_on_capitalised_titles_the_first_one_knew() -> None:
    for title in ("Kettle in brushed steel", "KEYBOARD with backlight",
                  "Travel Backpack", "Denim Jacket", "USB Cable"):
        assert categorise(title, V2) == categorise(title, V1), title


def test_every_model_is_loadable_by_the_version_the_deployment_names() -> None:
    assert {version: model.version for version, model in MODELS.items()} == {
        "v1": "v1", "v2": "v2"
    }

input.summary: Lowercase purchase titles before handing them to the categoriser, so v2 (which no longer folds case) recognises capitalised words
